message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need | How it works | |---------|---------------|--------------| | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue). Each color has numbers 0‑9 (two of each except one 0) and two of each action card: Skip, Reverse, Draw Two. Plus 4 Wild cards and 4 Wild Draw Four cards. | Shuffle the deck and deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down to form the draw pile. Turn the top card face‑up to start the discard pile. | | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or a pre‑agreed total). Points are tallied at the end of each round. | | **Gameplay** | 1. Play proceeds clockwise (unless a Reverse changes direction). 2. On your turn, you may play **one** card that matches either the color, number, or symbol of the top discard. 3. If you cannot play, you must draw one card from the draw pile. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction.
• **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – You choose the next color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – You choose the next color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. (Can only be played if you have no other playable card; otherwise, you can be challenged.) | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you play your second‑to‑last card, shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards all their cards. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of the cards left in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, action cards = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | | **Scoring** | Add the round score to the winner’s total. Play continues until someone reaches the target score (usually 500). | | **Optional Variations** | • **Stacking** – Allow players to stack Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards instead of drawing.
• **Custom Rules** – e.g., “Draw Two + Reverse” or “Wild Draw Four + Skip.”
• **House Rules** – e.g., “No Wild Draw Four on the first turn.” | **Quick Tips** - Keep an eye on the colors you’re running out of; try to hold a Wild card for a strategic switch. - Remember that a Wild Draw Four can only be played if you have no other playable card; otherwise, the next player can challenge you. - If the draw pile runs out, shuffle the discard pile (except the top card) to form a new draw pile. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
